events.artist: Boston Symphony Orchestra with Andris Nelsons & HIMARI
events.subtitle: All-Prokofiev: Violin Concerto No. 2 + Symphony No. 5
events.factual_description: Washington Performing Arts presents the Boston Symphony Orchestra at the Music Center at Strathmore on Monday, April 12, 2027 at 7:30 PM, conducted by Andris Nelsons with Japanese violinist HIMARI as soloist. The all-Prokofiev program pairs Violin Concerto No. 2 with Symphony No. 5. Washington Performing Arts states that this is the BSO's first return under Nelsons in its series since 2011. The BSO notes that it gave the American premieres of both works under Serge Koussevitzky, and that the same 2027 program also appears in Boston and at Carnegie Hall.

enrichment.note: Washington Performing Arts and HIMARI's official site independently verify the April 12 date, 7:30 PM time, Strathmore venue, Nelsons/BSO/HIMARI personnel and all-Prokofiev program. The authorized Washington Performing Arts ticket destination is exact and active. The HIMARI EP Apple Music destination is exact. No additional repertoire or personnel were inferred.

en.why_it_matters: This is an unusually clean intersection of the Japan thread and the local RADAR: HIMARI brings one of the most closely watched young Japanese violin voices to North Bethesda with Nelsons and the Boston Symphony, in a program that keeps the entire evening inside Prokofiev. The concerto puts tone, attack and long-line phrasing under a microscope; the Fifth Symphony then lets the same orchestra turn that language into mass and architecture. The BSO's own historical connection to the American premieres of both works gives the program an extra layer without turning it into heritage theater.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for this in the DMV. Strathmore gives the local calendar a first-rate orchestral date with a strong Japanese-instrumental thread, while the same program's Boston and Carnegie appearances mean there is no need to treat this stop as a scarcity event.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí se cruzan de forma muy limpia el hilo de Japón y el RADAR local: HIMARI trae a North Bethesda una de las voces jóvenes del violín japonés que más atención están generando, con Nelsons y la Boston Symphony, en un programa completamente metido en Prokófiev. El concierto obliga a escuchar tono, ataque y fraseo largo con lupa; después la Quinta Sinfonía deja que la misma orquesta convierta ese lenguaje en masa y arquitectura. La relación histórica de la BSO con los estrenos estadounidenses de ambas obras añade contexto sin volver la noche un ejercicio de museo.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente dentro del DMV. Strathmore gana una fecha orquestal de primer nivel con un hilo japonés e instrumental muy claro; como el mismo programa también pasa por Boston y Carnegie Hall, no hace falta tratar esta parada como un acontecimiento escaso.

events.subtitle: Final DC-area performances as Artistic Director — two distinct programs

priority_review.rationale: Washington Performing Arts explicitly identifies May 11 and May 13 as Wynton Marsalis's final DC-area performances as Artistic Director of Jazz at Lincoln Center, with two different programs, at the close of a more-than-four-decade relationship with the presenter that began in 1983. A+ would understate the specific farewell context and the genuine-regret value of missing the local closing chapter. S+ is not warranted because there are two performances and Marsalis's final season continues elsewhere, including later New York dates.

events.factual_description: Washington Performing Arts and Strathmore co-present the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis at the Music Center at Strathmore on Tuesday, May 11 and Thursday, May 13, 2027, both at 8:00 PM. Washington Performing Arts identifies these as Marsalis's final DC-area performances as Artistic Director of Jazz at Lincoln Center and Music Director of the Orchestra, closing a relationship with the presenter that dates to 1983. The two evenings will feature distinct programs emphasizing works by Marsalis and compositions and arrangements by JLCO members; detailed programs remain to be announced.

en.why_it_matters: This is the local closing chapter, not another JLCO tour stop. Washington Performing Arts first presented Marsalis in 1983; more than four decades later, these two different Strathmore programs are being presented explicitly as his final DC-area appearances in the role that shaped Jazz at Lincoln Center. That makes the institutional history part of the music: a band whose arranging language and ensemble discipline were built under Marsalis is closing a long Washington relationship by letting its own composers and arrangers share the frame with his work.
en.trip_verdict: Protect one of these nights in the DMV. If the two announced programs develop clearly different identities once repertoire is published, choosing between them will matter; until then, either date carries the farewell context strongly enough to anchor the local calendar.

es.why_it_matters: Éste sí es el cierre de un capítulo local, no otra parada de la JLCO. Washington Performing Arts presentó por primera vez a Marsalis en 1983; más de cuatro décadas después, estas dos noches distintas en Strathmore están planteadas explícitamente como sus últimas apariciones en el área de DC dentro del papel que definió Jazz at Lincoln Center. La historia institucional forma parte de la música: una orquesta cuyo lenguaje de arreglos y disciplina de ensamble se construyó bajo Marsalis cierra una relación larguísima con Washington dejando además espacio a las composiciones y arreglos de sus propios integrantes.
es.trip_verdict: Protegería una de estas dos noches dentro del DMV. Si cuando publiquen el repertorio los programas terminan teniendo identidades muy distintas, sí valdrá escoger con cuidado; por ahora cualquiera de las dos carga suficiente contexto de despedida para funcionar como una fecha-ancla local.
